parallel.requirements: Recognized pure Node ESM, .mjs suffixes, local imports only, manual argparse-like argv parsing, Bech32 checksum and verification behavior, Python-like list/boolean output, and /output delivery.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent retained implementation ownership while delegating CLI probing to a child; the child then spawned a nested CLI probe and wrote its own implementation files despite no clean file-ownership boundary.
parallel.implementation: Parent wrote Bech32, CLI, format, parse, root export, and test10 entry files; child later added alternate Bech32/parser/format/parse files and rewrote test10.mjs, after which parent consolidated and repaired the graph.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration happened through shared /output writes; parent found unexpected extra files, removed duplicate child modules, restored exports, and delivered a coherent final hierarchy with test10.mjs.
parallel.verification: Parent verified sample outputs, many argparse edge cases, negative-looking values, -- handling, help abbreviations, and post-repair sample/parser commands; official evaluator later reported 98/100.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No evaluator detail identifies the exact two failures, but the run had a transient broken module graph and coordination rework from overlapping child writes before final closure.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, local-only imports, manual argument parsing, Bech32 behavior, output formatting, /output placement, and executable probing requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, verification, final path normalization, and delivery without child delegation or shared-write coordination boundaries.
serial.implementation: Built a compact module tree for Bech32 constants/hrp/polymod/checksum, CLI argparse behavior, integer parsing, format helpers, and the test10 entry point.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Applied one coherent tree, then patched invalid integer handling and relative script invocation; final artifact list contains a single entry file and supporting modules.
serial.verification: Matched four provided samples, several parser success/error modes, help behavior, relative invocation, and 20 random executable comparisons; official evaluator later reported 98/100.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The mounted evidence does not expose the two failing hidden cases; the final status shows a completed but non-passing 98/100 solution.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed cell/status.json evaluation records both modes as solution_passed false with 98 passed of 100, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The concrete difference is process-level: parallel introduced child-side writes to the submitted entry file and overlapping modules, causing duplicate files, transient broken imports, and parent reconciliation; serial built and tested a single coherent tree. The mounted official evaluator evidence does not identify whether the two hidden failures are the same cases, so the retained parallel pattern is an adverse coordination episode, not an outcome-differential root cause.
parallel_contributors: Parent and child both wrote implementation files in /output, including the entry point, producing duplicate helper modules and a transient broken graph before final cleanup.
Parallel spent extra wait, follow-up, interruption, and repair steps around the child chain before closure.
serial_contributors: Serial kept all probing, implementation, integration, and verification in one actor with no child side effects.
Serial performed a 20-case random comparison in addition to samples and parser checks.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both final solutions still failed 2 of 100 official tests; the mounted evidence gives only aggregate counts and not the exact hidden failing inputs.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator summary is aggregate-only in the mounted pair, so failed-case identities cannot be attributed to one implementation detail from the available evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse process contributor, not an outcome differential
